title: Terrarium common types
description: Primitives shared by every Terrarium contract. Contract-wide rule: no floating-point numbers anywhere. Every number is an integer within the IEEE-754 safe range, so Rust, TypeScript and Python all read it exactly and canonical JSON is trivial.

SafeInt.description: Integer exactly representable in every JSON consumer (|n| <= 2^53 - 1).

Cents.description: Money in integer cents. Balances of ordinary accounts are never negative; only the boundary entity may go below zero.

Amount.description: A strictly positive amount of money in integer cents.

SimTime.description: Simulated seconds since the start of the run. Always a multiple of clock.tick_seconds once the kernel has stamped it. Never wall-clock time.

Duration.description: A span of simulated seconds. Durations are in seconds rather than ticks so configs survive a change of tick length; the kernel rounds up to whole ticks.

ConfigId.description: Identifier chosen by a researcher in a world config. Lowercase ASCII, no dots, so it can never collide with a kernel-generated id. Ids are unique across ALL kinds within a world (an entity and a seat cannot share an id).

KernelId.description: Identifier minted by the kernel: '<prefix>.<counter>', e.g. 'ent.12', 'agr.3'. Deterministic: counters live in world state.

Id.description: Any world identifier, researcher- or kernel-minted.

LocalRef.description: A name bound earlier in the same action by a block's 'ref' field, e.g. '$trust'. Lets one atomic action create something and then use it.

RefName.description: Declares a LocalRef; written without the '$'.

Text.description: Free text (messages, proposals, reasoning). Bounded to keep logs sane.

StructureCategory.description: What a structure is for; zoning is expressed in these.

RightKind.description: Rights are bundles, not simple ownership. surface = freehold of the surface; subsurface = minerals beneath; use = occupy and use (what a lease grants); access = pass through.

ParcelScope.description: Either every parcel in the issuer's jurisdiction, or an explicit list.

Opaque.description: Free-form data the kernel stores and logs but never interprets (controller params, annotation payloads). Still integer-only: floats are forbidden even here, because they would break canonical hashing across languages. Encode fractions as strings or scaled integers (e.g. temperature_milli: 700).
